name: Wild Berries
description: A handful of edible berries found in the underbrush.

name: Mushroom
description: A foraged mushroom. Some are filling, but eating the wrong one can make you sick.

name: Cooked Fish
description: A fish cooked over a fire. Restores hunger and is safer to eat than raw catch.

name: Raw Fish
description: A freshly caught fish. Can be cooked or eaten raw at a risk of sickness.

name: Dried Jerky
description: Preserved meat that stores well and restores a moderate amount of hunger.

name: Herbal Tea
description: A warm drink brewed from foraged herbs. Helps with thirst and mild sickness.

name: Bandage
description: A simple cloth wrap used to treat cuts and scrapes.

name: Stick
description: A sturdy wooden stick useful for crafting tools and starting fires.

name: Stone
description: A sharp or heavy stone that can be used as a tool or crafting component.

name: Plant Fiber
description: Tough plant fibers that can be twisted into cordage or used in bandages.

name: Flint
description: A hard stone that sparks when struck, useful for starting fires.

name: Fishing Rod
description: A simple rod for catching fish at lakes and rivers.

name: Hatchet
description: A small axe for chopping wood and gathering sticks more efficiently.

name: Campfire
description: A fire that provides warmth, light at night, and a way to cook food.

name: Makeshift Shelter
description: A crude lean-to that offers protection from weather and a place to rest.
